set.summary: The owner and the orchestrator (Claude Code in Rex) planned milestone 2 inside Genesis on 2026-10-25, right after milestone 1's import. Decided: milestone 2 is "Genesis runs the work" (layers 3–4), so milestone 3 is built with Genesis orchestrating; milestone 2 is an intent its change sets serve, with done points as child intents verified by Evidence; depends-on means only "can't start before", so the area chain is retired and the areas become a backlog; milestone work is carved out of the area bundles; a write sees the change sets it depends on, change sets land in dependency order, dropped dependencies and cycles are reported, rebasing stays manual; the scope (Claude Code adapter, runs with a built-in ship-change workflow, messages to a running step, interview answers as Decisions, blocked runs that tell the owner) and what is out; shipit stays the agent step; eight change sets, with 1, 2 and 7 written in full first and 3, 4, 5 and 8 proposed with intent only; the owner gave the go-ahead to accept 1, 2 and 7. Every answer was the owner accepting the orchestrator's proposal; the proposals' wording is the orchestrator's. Later: carving as decided couldn't be done with today's Genesis (re-creating a bundle's node changes its ID), so the owner added change set 9, carving that keeps IDs: carve by node, two entries with the same node and link IDs, the source made to depend on the target, its rules, and 3, 4, 5 and 8 depending on it. Then the product was renamed Rhiza (from mycorrhiza, the fungal network under a forest), chosen over Hypha and Myco because neither collides with an agent tool; the rename is change set 10: everything renamed, the log's history left as written, check identifying entries by ID and bytes, a clean break with one error for an old .genesis/ folder.

fields.quote: Ok I think I like the name. The designs are going to need some work but we've got a good start. I'm going to table that for now, but let's move forward with the name change.
fields.statement: The product is renamed Rhiza, from mycorrhiza, the fungal network that connects a forest; Hypha and Myco were set aside because each collides with an existing agent tool.
